s: As of June 2026, how many Ramsar sites did India have?
x: India had 100 Ramsar sites covering about 14 lakh hectares in June 2026, ranking first in Asia and third in the world.

s: The Ramsar Convention, under which wetlands are designated as Ramsar Sites, was adopted in which year?
x: The Ramsar Convention was adopted in 1971. India became a party to it in 1982.

s: On which date did India become a party to the Ramsar Convention?
x: India joined on 1 February 1982; 1971 is the year the Convention was signed and 1981 the year of the first Indian sites.

s: Which country took over the Ramsar Convention presidency for 2025–2028, after China?
x: Zimbabwe, host of COP15 at Victoria Falls, took over the presidency for 2025–2028 after China.

s: Which of the following was recognised as a new Ramsar Wetland City at Ramsar COP15 (2025)?
x: New Wetland Cities at COP15 were Victoria Falls (Zimbabwe), Kasane-Kazungula and Shakawe (Botswana).

s: Which of the following statements about Jayaprakash Narayan Bird Sanctuary (Surha Tal) is incorrect?
o: It is located in Ballia district of Uttar Pradesh.
It became India’s 100th Ramsar Site in June 2026.
It is a saline wetland located in Aligarh district.
x: The incorrect statement is that Surha Tal is a saline wetland located in Aligarh district. It is a freshwater wetland in Ballia district of Uttar Pradesh; Shekha Jheel Bird Sanctuary is located in Aligarh and was India’s 99th Ramsar Site.

s: After the addition of Jayaprakash Narayan Bird Sanctuary (Surha Tal), what was Uttar Pradesh's position and total number of Ramsar Sites?
o: Second after Tamil Nadu, with 13 sites
Second after Tamil Nadu, with 20 sites
Third after Tamil Nadu, with 13 sites

s: Which State has the highest number of Ramsar Sites in India, with 20 sites?
x: Tamil Nadu has the highest number of Ramsar Sites in India, with 20.

s: Where is Patna Bird Sanctuary, one of India's 97th–98th Ramsar sites, located?
x: Despite its name, Patna Bird Sanctuary is in Etah, Uttar Pradesh, not in Bihar.

s: What type of wetland is Surha Tal (Jayaprakash Narayan Bird Sanctuary), India's 100th Ramsar site?
x: Surha Tal in Ballia is a freshwater wetland, not saline; it supports groundwater recharge and fisheries.

s: Which Ramsar site was designated in Chhattisgarh in 2025?
x: Kopra Jalsahay, also called Kopra Reservoir, was designated as a Ramsar site in Chhattisgarh in 2025. Gogul Jalsahay is the similarly named site associated with Bihar.

s: Which Ramsar Sites were added on World Environment Day, 5 June 2025?
o: Patna Bird Sanctuary and Chhari-Dhand Wetland
x: Menar Wetland and Khichan Wetland were added on 5 June 2025, observed as World Environment Day. Gokul Reservoir and Udaipur Jheel were added in September 2025, while Siliserh Lake and Kopra Reservoir were added in December 2025.

s: In which State is Udhwa Lake, a Ramsar site, located?

o: Patna Bird Sanctuary and Goga Beel Lake
Chhari-Dhand Wetland and Goga Beel Lake
Patna Bird Sanctuary and Chhari-Dhand Wetland
x: Patna Bird Sanctuary and Chhari-Dhand Wetland were India's 97th and 98th Ramsar Sites on World Wetlands Day 2026. Goga Beel Lake was added in October 2025, while Siliserh Lake and Kopra Reservoir were added in December 2025.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's Ramsar sites added in 2026?
o: Shekha Jheel Bird Sanctuary was added on 22 April 2026
Shekha Jheel Bird Sanctuary took India's Ramsar total to 99
Shekha Jheel Bird Sanctuary took India's Ramsar total to 98

s: Which of the following Ramsar site–district pairs (added 2025) is correctly matched?

s: Which is the only Ramsar site in Andhra Pradesh, designated in 2002?
x: Kolleru Lake is the only Ramsar site in Andhra Pradesh and was designated in 2002. Chilika Lake is in Odisha, Renuka Wetland is in Himachal Pradesh, and Sundarbans is in West Bengal.

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about India's Ramsar-site records?

s: Chilika Lake, a Ramsar site designated in 1981, is located in which State?

s: In which year were Loktak, Harike, Sambhar and Wular lakes all included in India's Ramsar list?

x: Point Calimere Wildlife & Bird Sanctuary is Tamil Nadu’s oldest Ramsar site. The other options are later entries in the listed Ramsar-site chronology.

x: Vembannur (Tamil Nadu) is now the smallest; Renuka (Himachal Pradesh) was the smallest earlier, and Sundarbans is the largest.

s: Which is the largest Ramsar site in India?
x: The Sundarbans Wetland (West Bengal, 2019) is India's largest Ramsar site.

s: Which were India's first Ramsar sites, designated in 1981?

s: The national fish of India is
x:
Official key / most books: Indian Mackerel. Strictly: the Government of India has not notified any national fish (the Ganges river dolphin is the national aquatic animal; Golden Mahseer has only been proposed) — web search found no official listing.
Exam keys and GK books give the Indian Mackerel as India's national fish, so it is keyed. Hilsa is the State Fish of West Bengal and the National Fish of Bangladesh; Pomfret and Rohu are not national symbols.

s: Plachimada which has been in the news for immense damage to its environment lies in –
x: Plachimada is a small village in Palakkad district of Kerala. It is situated in Chittur block’s Perumatty Panchayat of the district. In 2000, this Panchayat gave license to the Hindustan Coca-Cola Beverages Private Limited (HCCBPL) to manufacture Coca-Cola (Coke) and other products viz. Fanta, Limca, Thums Up, Sprite, Kinley, etc. But very soon due to the contamination of groundwater in that locality by the chemical waste discharged by the company, local people started a small-scale protest against the company. Later, this protest was supported by the Panchayat authorities. In the long run, with national as well as international support to this protest against a multinational company (MNC), this movement became an icon of other such movements worldwide.
